title: Review of the free-predator test on fresh seed 9 (256^2): replicates closely; 13% of predator bodies free, 250 of 317 detachments end in dissolution while free, 0 hops, 0 of 40 divisions with a free parent
summary: Applied c56's freepred.py, unchanged, to my own labkit run of the digestion-ecology world on fresh seed 9 (256^2, defaults, t=12000; the run of 20261027T0851-c55-review-digestion-ecology). From t=2500: mean 187 predator bodies, 24 free (gap > 2 px) per frame (free fraction 0.13, claim 0.14); 317 detachments, of which 250 end with the body gone while free, 51 reattach and 16 are free at the end; free spells median 5 frames (500 t), max 12 (1200 t); 0 hops between prey; 40 predator divisions, none with a free parent or a parent more than 6 px from prey, 5 with a daughter free 500 t later (1 with both).

observations.I: free_s9.json: free_frac 0.131, detach_events 317, spell_fates reattach 51 / end 250 / alive_at_end 16, hops 0, divisions 40, div_parent_free 0, div_parent_gap_gt6 0, div_any_kid_free_t5 5. Consistent with my own partner count on the same run (20261027T0851-c55-review-digestion-ecology/partners9.json: 302 of 306 long-lived predator tracks touch one prey lineage).

seeds_run.result: pass: free fraction 0.13, 250/317 detachments end dissolved, 0 hops, 0/40 divisions with a free parent

verdicts.limitation: Same script as the author, so its definitions are shared: a predator whose prey dissolves under it counts as detached, and tracks end at merges. I did not rerun the predator-free twin here (it is in my digestion review on the same seed) or the store variant. The result says predators do not live apart from prey; it does not by itself settle whether the pair or the predator is the individual: in my earlier review only 3 of 36 predator splits coincided with a prey split.
